Located in Hisar (Haryana), Rakhigarhi is the largest known archaeological site of the Indus-Saraswati Civilisation, spanning approximately 550 hectares, significantly larger than both Harappa and Mohenjo-daro. Major excavations at the site have revealed advanced urban planning, sophisticated craftsmanship, a large lapidary workshop, drainage systems, wells, and a substantial cemetery. Many scholars believe it may have served as a major provincial capital or an important regional center of the Indus-Saraswati Civilisation. These discoveries firmly establish that the heart and largest expanse of the Indus-Saraswati Civilisation thrived across a vast area of Bharat. Ongoing research and preservation efforts at Rakhigarhi continue to provide deeper insights into this ancient civilisation and its profound roots in Indian history. #Rakhigarhi #IndusSaraswatiCivilisation #LargestIndusSite #AncientIndianHeritage #CivilisationalContinuity @ASIGoI

HONOURING THE BRAVEHEARTS Certain reports circulating in sections of the media and on social media platforms have incorrectly suggested that the supreme sacrifice of six bravehearts during Operation Sindoor have been acknowledged or brought to public notice for the first time only recently. It is clarified that the nation paid homage to these fallen heroes at the earliest opportunity, well before the reports in question. During the official Press Conference held on 11 May 2025, then Director General of Military Operations (DGMO), paid solemn tribute to these brave soldiers and specifically acknowledged their sacrifice in the line of duty during Operation SINDOOR. These bravehearts were conferred with gallantry awards and this was published in the Press Release of 14 Aug 2025. This constituted a formal and National recognition of their valour and supreme sacrifice in keeping with the highest traditions of the Indian Defence Forces. Simultaneously, the Indian Army’s official social media platforms carried tributes to these bravehearts without delay. The nation’s recognition of these heroes has continued thereafter. During the Army Day Parade held at Jaipur on 15 January 2026, the Chief of the Army Staff (COAS) presented the Sena Medal (Gallantry) to the families of three of these gallant soldiers, while the Chief of Air Staff did the same on 08 Oct 2025 in a solemn ceremony, reaffirming the Defence Forces enduring commitment to honouring those who have laid down their lives in the service of the nation. With regard to the engraving of the names of fallen soldiers on the National War Memorial, it is emphasised that this sacred process is governed by an established and well-defined protocol. The Defence Forces follow these laid-down procedures with due diligence, care and reverence, commensurate with the solemnity of the honour being conferred. Any suggestion that due process was not followed is factually incorrect. It is regrettable that an avoidable and unfounded controversy has arisen around this issue. Such narratives not only misrepresent facts but also risk causing unnecessary anguish to bereaved families and detracting from the dignity owed to those who made the supreme sacrifice in service of the nation. All stakeholders are urged to exercise responsibility and restraint while reporting on matters relating to fallen soldiers and to refrain from disseminating unverified information. The Indian Defence Forces remains steadfast in its commitment to honouring every soldier who has offered supreme sacrifice in defence of the nation. The six bravehearts of Operation Sindoor are national heroes whose courage, devotion to duty and sacrifice will continue to inspire generations of Indians. Melting ice in the Arctic is opening access to critical materials and sharpening competition over resources. But this is also a health security issue, exposing how supply-chain shocks and changing ecosystems can affect the resilience of health systems. That was the focus of an important panel I joined at the @DubrovnikForum with Croatia’s Health Minister Dr Irena Hrstić; Japan’s State Minister for Foreign Affairs @ayano_kunimitsu; Co-founder and Secretary-General of @CCG_org @mabelmiaoccg; and Senior Fellow at the Hudson Institute’s Center on Europe & Eurasia @dankochis. These questions are not distant for health. Shortages of medicines, medical equipment or essential resources can quickly affect whether people receive the care they need. I stressed that a truly resilient health system is one that responds to the immediate crisis while continuing essential care for people with ongoing needs, from a child with cancer to an older person with dementia or a pregnant woman preparing to give birth. To make this a reality, we need to support health workers, including their mental health and well-being; strengthen primary health care close to communities; and build trust between citizens, health workers and governments. This is where @WHO has a unique role. No country holds all the answers, but every country has experience others can learn from. WHO helps connect that knowledge, make it available to all Member States, and ensure it is guided by science, transparency, and trust. That is also why equity matters. Global health security is only strong when knowledge, preparedness and care reach every country and every community, leaving no one behind.

Located in Hisar (Haryana), Rakhigarhi is the largest known archaeological site of the Indus-Saraswati Civilisation, spanning approximately 550 hectares, significantly larger than both Harappa and Mohenjo-daro. Major excavations at the site have revealed advanced urban planning, sophisticated craftsmanship, a large lapidary workshop, drainage systems, wells, and a substantial cemetery. Many scholars believe it may have served as a major provincial capital or an important regional center of the Indus-Saraswati Civilisation. These discoveries firmly establish that the heart and largest expanse of the Indus-Saraswati Civilisation thrived across a vast area of Bharat. Ongoing research and preservation efforts at Rakhigarhi continue to provide deeper insights into this ancient civilisation and its profound roots in Indian history. #Rakhigarhi #IndusSaraswatiCivilisation #LargestIndusSite #AncientIndianHeritage #CivilisationalContinuity

🇦🇫 | L’Émirat islamique d’Afghanistan a ordonné une interdiction nationale de l’utilisation des smartphones par les fonctionnaires. Selon une ordonnance citée par Reuters, l’utilisation des smartphones sera interdite à partir du 16 juin pour tous les responsables des institutions militaires et civiles, y compris les juges. Un rapport du Afghan Analysts Network a interviewé des combattants taliban devenus bureaucrates, qui se plaignaient de passer des heures à scroller sur X. « Ils détestent la culture de bureau. Ils se plaignaient en permanence. Ils regrettent le champ de bataille. » Une autre source consultée par Arab Intelligence indique que les fonctionnaires utilisent leurs smartphones pour photographier des documents et enregistrer des réunions, laissant filtrer des informations avant même que le Guide suprême ne les signe. 📝 Formellement sécuritaire, la mesure est structurellement un outil de verrouillage idéologique, couper les fonctionnaires de sources d’information exogènes, neutraliser les fuites vers les médias et les ONG, et tester la loyauté par soumission ostentatoire (vidéos de smartphones écrasés publiées en ligne par des commandants). Le calendrier, entrée en vigueur le 1er Mouharram (16 juin) ajoute une dimension symbolique qui pourrait suggérer une interprétation salafiste/déobandie de « tajdid » (renouveau) au début de l’année islamique.
